analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: one added configuration-table row at head line 1090, describing prompt-chunk attention in 128-query blocks. It also describes a fused-causal prefill fast path for full-attention chunks (no window, softcap, vision span or bidirectional mask; fused head_dim values) and the `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL=0` rollback. No executable code, wire contract, key handling, attestation, authorization or cache-storage logic is touched. The supplied units are base-side text (lines 1638-2205) outside the changed range, so I examined them as surrounding context only. The changed row itself is visible only in the patch excerpt.

Security relevance: the row describes a prefill attention optimization in TB-007 (inference engine). The documented fast path applies to the same full-attention chunks, so it should not alter T-041 (prefix-cache/SSD tier, HMAC names, TTL, scope salt) or A-001 plaintext exposure. Prefill timing could shift, which affects the TTFT oracle only marginally and stays under the accepted SEC-035 risk. The doc states the fast path excludes vision spans and bidirectional masks. It keeps its own path for live packed paged KV, and the env kill switch restores block mode.

Remaining questions for source review: whether the underlying AttentionV1.swift and PagedLayerCache.swift change, which is not in this batch, preserves memory admission and the causal mask semantics across requests in a batch. A mask error there would be a correctness and isolation risk (T-028/T-041), but nothing in the supplied docs shows a regression. No threat-model update is needed from this documentation-only change.
